overview: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa. Apart from a short Atlantic coastline, it is completely surrounded by Senegal. Its capital is Banjul. The Gambia became independent from the United Kingdom in 1965, and English is the official language.

geography.text: The Gambia is a narrow strip of land on both banks of the Gambia River, stretching around 300 kilometres inland but never more than about 50 kilometres wide. The land is low and flat, with mangroves and wetlands near the river and savanna further from it.

history.text: The Gambia River was part of the Mali Empire's trade routes, and later of the Atlantic slave trade. Britain built a fort on an island in the river and took control of the land along its banks, which is why the country is a long, thin strip surrounded by Senegal. The Gambia became independent in 1965.

events.title: Kunta Kinteh Island
events.text: European traders use a fort on the river as a slave-trading post.

events.title: Senegambia
events.text: A short-lived confederation with Senegal begins.

events.title: Change of power
events.text: Yahya Jammeh leaves after losing an election.

government.text: The Gambia is a presidential republic. Yahya Jammeh ruled for 22 years until he lost an election in 2016 and left after a regional intervention. Since then the country has held peaceful elections.

economy.text: Farming, especially groundnuts, tourism and money from Gambians abroad support the economy.

culture.text: The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa, a narrow strip along the Gambia River surrounded by Senegal. Griots, storytellers and musicians, keep oral history alive, and the kora, a 21-string harp-lute, is a national instrument. The book Roots traced its author's ancestry to Juffureh.

items.title: Kunta Kinteh Island
items.text: A former slave-trading post, listed by UNESCO.

sport.text: Football and wrestling are popular. The Gambia reached the quarter-finals of the Africa Cup of Nations at its first attempt in 2022.

items.text: Africa Cup of Nations quarter-finalists at the first attempt.
